title: Mitigated API Authentication Bypass Vulnerability in python.org Download Metadata
summary: The Python Security Response Team (PSRT) addressed an authentication bypass vulnerability in python.org's release management API, reported by DEVCORE Research Team. The flaw, present since 2014, could have allowed attackers to modify release metadata (e.g., download URLs and verification materials) but not the release files themselves. No exploitation was detected after thorough audits of logs, database backups, and verification of Sigstore/PGP materials. Patches were deployed within 48 hours, and additional hardening measures were implemented, including HTTPS enforcement, URL validation, and extended logging retention.
key_points: Vulnerability: Authentication bypass in python.org's release management API (CVE not mentioned but present since 2014).
Impact: Attackers could modify metadata (e.g., download URLs, verification materials) but not release files directly.
Exploitation: No evidence of exploitation found after auditing logs, database backups, and Sigstore/PGP verification.
Remediation: Patch deployed within 48 hours to separate guest and API key authentication modes.
Hardening Measures: HTTPS enforcement, URL validation (rejecting non-python.org URLs), and extended logging retention (30 days).
Audits: Manual and LLM-assisted code audits, plus a third-party audit by Trail of Bits, found no additional issues.
Timeline: Reported on February 23, 2026; patch confirmed by February 24; final report published on June 23.
Acknowledgements: DEVCORE Research Team for disclosure, OpenAI for funding the audit, and Trail of Bits for the audit.
